--- title: "Salary value: who is over- or underpaid?" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Takeaways - **The old ratio rule labeled most players.** The notebook's rule (predicted ÷ actual salary above 1.2 or below 0.8) called 38% of NBA veterans underpaid and 37% overpaid. With 90% intervals, only 6% and 4% are clearly over- or underpaid; for everyone else the difference is within the model's uncertainty. - **Max contracts can't be judged against the market.** The old rule called 72% of NBA max-contract players overpaid, but max pay is capped by the league's rules, so their market value is never observed. They're shown by value delivered instead. - **Minimum contracts are underpaid by design**, especially late-season prorated deals. - **Injuries:** each overpay is split into a part from games missed and a part from performance. ::: ## How it works - **Pay scale:** salary as a share of an average team payroll in that league-season. This puts the NBA, WNBA and every season on one scale without typing in salary-cap figures. - **Seasons:** NBA 2009-10 onward, WNBA 2021 onward (when salary data is complete). - **Fair pay:** a gradient-boosting model of pay, trained only on **veteran** contracts, because rookie-scale, minimum and max salaries are set by rules. Inputs: lineup-based offense and defense impact (this season and last), minutes (this season and last), availability, age, position and archetype. More impact, minutes or availability never lowers fair pay. Each player's own season is held out when predicting him. - **Surplus:** log(fair pay) − log(actual pay); above 0 = underpaid. Never a ratio. - **Interval:** a 90% band for fair pay, calibrated on held-out seasons (it covers 90% of NBA and WNBA veteran contracts). A player is labeled only when the whole band is on one side of zero. - **Low-salary shrinkage:** the surplus on cheap contracts was shrunk by a factor tuned with cross-validation (does the shrunk surplus predict the pay change at a player's next contract?). The tuning chose **no shrinkage**, so cheap contracts are instead kept in their own cohort. - **Contract cohorts:** rookie scale (draft history, plus inferred for 2024+ draftees), minimum scale (identical low amounts paid to many players, or prorated deals), max scale (identical top-tier amounts), veteran. ## Who is clearly over- or underpaid, by contract type Each bar is the share of player-seasons the model is confident about: **underpaid to the right, overpaid to the left**. Everyone else (the large majority) is paid within what the model can tell apart. ```{=html}
``` **What this shows:** minimum-contract players are the most often underpaid (their pay is set by the league's minimum, not by how good they are). Veterans and rookies are mostly paid about right: only around one in twenty is clearly off in either direction. Max contracts show no bars because their pay is capped by rule, so they are judged by value delivered instead (table further down). **Old ratio rule vs the new interval rule.** The old rule (predicted ÷ actual pay above 1.2 or below 0.8) flags far more players because it ignores uncertainty: | league | contract type | player-seasons | old rule: under | old rule: over | new rule: under | new rule: over | |:---------|:----------------|-----------------:|:------------------|:-----------------|:------------------|:-----------------| | NBA | max scale | 499 | 4% | 72% | 0% | 0% | | NBA | minimum scale | 1461 | 84% | 5% | 44% | 0% | | NBA | rookie scale | 1617 | 39% | 40% | 5% | 5% | | NBA | veteran | 3783 | 38% | 37% | 6% | 4% | | WNBA | max scale | 75 | 0% | 72% | 0% | 0% | | WNBA | minimum scale | 199 | 63% | 6% | 35% | 0% | | WNBA | rookie scale | 134 | 25% | 10% | 7% | 1% | | WNBA | veteran | 483 | 30% | 28% | 6% | 4% | ## Has the 2023 CBA (second apron) changed who is overpaid? The 2023 CBA took effect on July 1, 2023 (the 2023-24 season) and added a **second apron**, a payroll line above the luxury tax. Teams over it lose tools to add or keep players: no taxpayer mid-level exception, no aggregating salaries in trades, no using older trade exceptions, no sending cash in trades. The restrictions phased in over two seasons and were fully in force from 2024-25 ([Hoops Rumors glossary](https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/01/hoops-rumors-glossary-tax-aprons-2.html); [theScore](https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/2940429)). | contract type | period | player-seasons | clearly underpaid | clearly overpaid | typical surplus (log) | typical pay (share of avg payroll) | |:----------------|:------------------------------|-----------------:|:--------------------|:-------------------|------------------------:|:-------------------------------------| | max scale | 2016-17 to 2022-23 (old CBA) | 201 | 0.0% | 0.0% | -0.53 | 25.9% | | max scale | 2023-24 to 2025-26 (2023 CBA) | 124 | 0.0% | 0.0% | -0.38 | 25.3% | | minimum scale | 2016-17 to 2022-23 (old CBA) | 612 | 43.5% | 0.0% | 0.89 | 1.1% | | minimum scale | 2023-24 to 2025-26 (2023 CBA) | 263 | 51.7% | 0.0% | 1.05 | 1.1% | | rookie scale | 2016-17 to 2022-23 (old CBA) | 643 | 3.9% | 4.8% | -0.07 | 3.0% | | rookie scale | 2023-24 to 2025-26 (2023 CBA) | 329 | 4.0% | 3.6% | 0.02 | 2.7% | | veteran | 2016-17 to 2022-23 (old CBA) | 1610 | 6.8% | 5.7% | 0.01 | 6.6% | | veteran | 2023-24 to 2025-26 (2023 CBA) | 646 | 6.8% | 1.5% | 0.08 | 5.9% | **What this shows:** the new CBA has *not* led to more overpaid role players; if anything the opposite. Since 2023-24, the share of veterans clearly overpaid fell from 5.7% to 1.5%, and the typical veteran now delivers about 9% more value than his pay (about even before), while veterans' typical pay fell from 6.6% to 5.9% of an average payroll. Minimum-contract players are underpaid more often (44% → 52%), and max players' typical shortfall narrowed (-0.53 → -0.38). That fits teams near the aprons squeezing the middle of the salary scale and filling rosters with cheaper contracts. It is three seasons of data and an association, not proof that the apron caused it. ## Clearly over- or underpaid veterans, latest season Only players whose 90% interval excludes zero. *Surplus* is in
